confidence_notes: I ran 5 web searches: 1 for the RBA rate and 4 for Arica prices. No source gave a current Arica-specific figure for every drink or meal item. Coffee and inexpensive-meal anchors rest on aggregator figures that are partly stale. Those were a roughly CLP 3,000-3,300 cappuccino, a CLP 5,000 meal (Numbeo-derived, early 2024), and a Jobicy estimate of about $2.50 for coffee and about $8 for a meal. The beer anchor draws on an Expatistan pub average of about CLP 2,830 (undated) and a Chile-wide table showing CLP 4,000 for local draft. I raised it to reflect restaurant pricing in 2026. I found no Arica prices for cocktails or wine by the glass. Those two anchors are set from their usual relationship to beer in Chilean restaurants, with the pisco sour a little above beer and the glass of wine near it. I assumed roughly CLP 930-950 per USD, which I did not verify. The mid-range two-person meal is a bounded estimate scaled from the inexpensive meal, not a sourced price. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of northern Chile and Arica's modest, domestic-and-border tourism market. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Arica is a mid-sized, lower-cost northern Chilean coastal city near the Peruvian border. I priced it below Santiago and tourist-heavy Chilean destinations, and somewhat above Peruvian border cities such as Tacna. Beer, coffee and restaurant anchors were scaled from Chile-wide and Arica-specific aggregator figures.
